entries.name: Linux Ptrace Argument PTRACE_CONT
entries.description: Restart the stopped tracee process.

entries.name: Linux Ptrace Argument PTRACE_GETREGS
entries.description: Copy the tracee's general-purpose or floating-point registers, respectively, to the address data in the tracer.

entries.name: Linux Ptrace Argument PTRACE_INTERRUPT
entries.description: Stops a tracee.

entries.name: Linux Ptrace Argument PTRACE_PEEKTEXT
entries.description: Read a word at the address addr in the tracee's memory, returning the word as the result of the ptrace() call.

entries.name: Linux Ptrace Argument PTRACE_POKETEXT
entries.description: Copy the word data to the address addr in the tracee's memory.

entries.name: Linux Ptrace Argument PTRACE_SETREGS
entries.description: Modify the tracee's general-purpose or floating-point registers, respectively, from the address data in the tracer.

entries.name: Linux Ptrace Argument PTRACE_DETACH
entries.description: Restart the stopped tracee as for PTRACE_CONT, but first detach from it.

entries.name: Linux Ptrace Argument PTRACE_TRACEME
entries.description: Indicates that the process is to be traced by its parent.

entries.name: Linux Read
entries.description: Read from a file descriptor.

entries.name: Linux Readv
entries.description: Read data into multiple buffers.

entries.name: Linux Rename
entries.description: Change the name or location of a file.

entries.name: Linux Renameat
entries.description: Change the name or location of a file. Different parameter handling than Linux Rename.

entries.name: Linux Renameat2
entries.description: Change the name or location of a file. Additional flags argument.

entries.name: Linux Socket
entries.description: Create an endpoint for communication.

entries.name: Linux Time
entries.description: Get time in seconds.

entries.name: Linux Unlink
entries.description: Delete a name and possibly the file it refers to.

entries.name: Linux Unlinkat
entries.description: Delete a name and possibly the file it refers to. Different parameter handling than Linux Unlink

entries.name: Linux Vfork
entries.description: Create child process that temp suspends parent process until it terminates.

entries.name: Linux Write
entries.description: Write to a file descriptor.

entries.name: Linux Writev
entries.description: Write data into multiple buffers.

entries.name: Linux _Exit
entries.description: Terminate the calling process.

entries.name: Load Library Event
entries.description: An event where a process dynamically loads a library or module into its memory space, extending its capabilities.

entries.name: Load Module
entries.description: A system call that loads a driver or extension into the kernel.

entries.name: Local Account Monitoring
entries.description: Analyzing local user accounts to detect unauthorized activity.

entries.name: Local Area Network
entries.description: A local area network (LAN) is a computer network that interconnects computers within a limited area such as a residence, school, laboratory, university campus or office building and has its network equipment and interconnects locally managed. Ethernet and Wi-Fi are the two most common transmission technologies in use for local area networks. Historical technologies include ARCNET, Token ring, and AppleTalk.

entries.name: Local Area Network Attacker
entries.description: An attacker who exploits vulnerabilities within the same local area network.

entries.name: Local Area Network Traffic
entries.description: Intranet local area network (LAN) traffic is network traffic that does not cross a given network's boundaries; where that network is defined as a LAN.

entries.name: Local Attacker
entries.description: An attacker who is physically near or on the premises of the target network or systems.

entries.name: Local Authentication Service
entries.description: A local authentication service running on a host can authenticate a user logged into just that local host computer.

entries.name: Local Authorization Service
entries.description: A local authorization service running on a host can authorize a user logged into just that local host computer.

entries.name: Local File Access Mediation
entries.description: Local file access mediation is the process of an operating system granting or denying a specific access request to a local file.

entries.name: Local File Permissions
entries.description: Local file permissions is the systematic process of defining, implementing, and managing access control policies that dictate user permissions for accessing files on a local system through the configuration of operating system functionality.

entries.name: Local Resource
entries.description: In computing, a system resource, or simply resource, is any physical or virtual component of limited availability within a computer system. Every device connected to a computer system is a resource. Every internal system component is a resource. Virtual system resources include files (concretely file handles), network connections (concretely network sockets), and memory areas. Managing resources is referred to as resource management, and includes both preventing resource leaks (releasing a resource when a process has finished using it) and dealing with resource contention (when multiple processes wish to access a limited resource).

entries.name: Local Resource Access
entries.description: Ephemeral digital artifact comprising a request of a local resource and any response from that resource.

entries.name: Local User Account
entries.description: A user account on a given host is a local user account for that specific host.

entries.name: Log
entries.description: A record of events in the order of their occurrence.

entries.name: Log File
entries.description:
A log file is a file that records either events that occur in an operating system or other software runs, or messages between different users of a communication software. Logging is the act of keeping a log. In the simplest case, messages are written to a single log file.

A transaction log is a file (i.e., log) of the communications between a system and the users of that system, or a data collection method that automatically captures the type, content, or time of transactions made by a person from a terminal with that system. For Web searching, a transaction log is an electronic record of interactions that have occurred during a searching episode between a Web search engine and users searching for information on that Web search engine.

Many operating systems, software frameworks and programs include a logging system. A widely used logging standard is syslog, defined in Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) RFC 5424). The syslog standard enables a dedicated, standardized subsystem to generate, filter, record, and analyze log messages. This relieves software developers of having to design and code their own ad hoc logging systems.

entries.name: Log Message Function
entries.description: Produces an entry in a log.

entries.name: Logic Programming
entries.description: Logic programming is a programming paradigm which is largely based on formal logic.

entries.name: Logical Link
entries.description: A Logical Link is an abstract or virtual connection between two entities that facilitates communication or data exchange without requiring a direct physical connection.

entries.name: Logical Link Mapping
entries.description: Logical link mapping creates a model of existing or previous node-to-node connections using network-layer data or metadata.

entries.name: Logical Rules
entries.description: A logical rule matches event data or set of values to a conditional expression and results in the determination of a truth value, which may be used to determine the next action or step to take.

entries.name: Login Session
entries.description: In computing, a login session is the period of activity between a user logging in and logging out of a (multi-user) system. This includes local login sessions, where a user has direct physical access to a computer, as well as domain login sessions, where a user logs into a computer that is part of a network domain.

entries.name: Logistic Regression
entries.description: Logistic regression is estimating the parameters of a logistic model.

entries.name: Logistic Regression Learning
entries.description: A supervised learning method that builds a logistic regression model using training data.

entries.name: Logoff Event
entries.description: An authentication event where an active session is conclusively terminated, resulting in the cessation of access and deallocation of resources associated with the session, ensuring that the connection to the system, application, or resource no longer exists.

entries.name: Logon Event
entries.description: An authentication event where a new session is initiated, signifying the successful validation of credentials and establishment of an authorized connection to a system, application, or resource. This marks the beginning of the subject’s authenticated interaction with the system.

entries.name: Long Short-term Memory
entries.description: Unlike standard feedforward neural networks, LSTM has feedback connections. Such a recurrent neural network (RNN) can process not only single data points (such as images), but also entire sequences of data (such as speech or video). This characteristic makes LSTM networks ideal for processing and predicting data

entries.name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
Disable or Remove Feature or Program
MAC Address
entries.description: A media access control address (MAC address) is a unique identifier assigned to a network interface controller (NIC) for use as a network address in communications within a network segment.

entries.name: MacOS Keychain
entries.description: Keychain is the password management system in macOS, developed by Apple. It was introduced with Mac OS 8.6, and has been included in all subsequent versions of the operating system, now known as macOS. A Keychain can contain various types of data: passwords (for websites, FTP servers, SSH accounts, network shares, wireless networks, groupware applications, encrypted disk images), private keys, certificates, and secure notes.

entries.name: Machine Learning
entries.description: Machine learning techniques are computational methods that combine statistics, probability, and optimization to make accurate predictions and/or improve performance.

entries.name: Mail Network Traffic
entries.description: Mail traffic is network traffic that uses a standard mail transfer protocol.

entries.name: Mail Server
entries.description: Within the Internet email system, a message transfer agent or mail transfer agent (MTA) or mail relay is software that transfers electronic mail messages from one computer to another using SMTP. The terms mail server, mail exchanger, and MX host are also used in some contexts. Messages exchanged across networks are passed between mail servers, including any attached data files (such as images, multimedia or documents). These servers also often keep mailboxes for email. Access to this email by end users is typically either via webmail or an email client.

entries.name: Mail Service
entries.description: A mail service provides the ability to send and receive mail across a computer network.  The mail service runs on message transfer agents (i.e., mail servers) and is accessed by users through an email client.

entries.name: Mathematical Function
entries.description: Computes mathematical expressions.

entries.name: Maximum-margin Learning
entries.description: Maximum-margin classifiers attempt to maximize the distance between the given data points and the decision boundary

entries.name: Mean
entries.description: The sum of all measurements divided by the number of observations in the data set.

entries.name: Mean Absolute Deviation
entries.description: The mean absolute deviation (MAD), also referred to as the "mean deviation" or sometimes "average absolute deviation", is the mean of the data's absolute deviations around the data's mean: the average (absolute) distance from the mean.

entries.name: Media Server
entries.description: A media server is a computer appliance or an application software that stores digital media (video, audio or images) and makes it available over a network. Media servers range from servers that provide video on demand to smaller personal computers or NAS (Network Attached Storage) for the home.

entries.name: Median
entries.description: The middle value that separates the higher half from the lower half of the data set. The median and the mode are the only measures of central tendency that can be used for ordinal data, in which values are ranked relative to each other but are not measured absolutely.

entries.name: Median Absolute Deviation
entries.description: The median absolute deviation (also MAD) is the median of the absolute deviation from the median.

entries.name: Memory Address
entries.description: In computing, a memory address is a reference to a specific memory location used at various levels by software and hardware.

entries.name: Memory Address Space
entries.description: A memory address space is a space containing memory addresses.

entries.name: Memory Allocation Event
entries.description: An event representing the allocation of memory resources to a process, providing it with the capacity to store data or execute instructions.

entries.name: Memory Allocation Function
entries.description: Reserves memory for a running process to use.

entries.name: Memory Block
entries.description: In computing (specifically data transmission and data storage), a block, sometimes called a physical record, is a sequence of bytes or bits, usually containing some whole number of records, having a maximum length; a block size. Data thus structured are said to be blocked. The process of putting data into blocks is called blocking, while deblocking is the process of extracting data from blocks. Blocked data is normally stored in a data buffer and read or written a whole block at a time.

entries.name: Memory Block Start Validation
entries.description: Ensuring that a pointer accurately references the beginning of a designated memory block.

entries.name: Memory Boundary Tracking
entries.description: Analyzing a call stack for return addresses which point to unexpected  memory locations.

entries.name: Memory Deletion Event
entries.description: An event marking the release or deallocation of memory resources, reclaiming them for reuse within the system.

entries.name: Memory Device Event
entries.description: An event describing activity in primary storage devices, such as DRAM or SRAM memory initialization, reconfiguration, or failures.

entries.name: Memory Event
entries.description: An event capturing operations on the memory resources of a system, encompassing allocation, modification, access, protection, or deallocation.

entries.name: Memory Extent
entries.description: A memory extent is a defined, contiguous region of memory within a computing system, characterized by its size, location, and purpose. It represents an abstraction of physical or virtual memory used for storing data, instructions, or other computational artifacts.

entries.name: Memory Free Function
entries.description: Releases previously reserved memory associated with a process.

entries.name: Memory Management Unit
entries.description: A computer’s memory management unit (MMU) is the physical hardware that handles its virtual memory and caching operations. The MMU is usually located within the computer’s central processing unit (CPU), but sometimes operates in a separate integrated chip (IC).

entries.name: Memory Management Unit Component
entries.description: A Memory Management Unit Component is a hardware or software element that contributes to the functionality of a Memory Management Unit, which is responsible for managing and translating memory addresses in a computing system.

entries.name: Memory Map Event
entries.description: An event representing the mapping of memory regions into a process's virtual address space, enabling efficient access to shared or reserved memory.

entries.name: Memory Modification Event
entries.description: An event where a process modifies allocated memory, potentially altering its content, behavior, or state.

entries.name: Memory Pool
entries.description: Memory pools, also called fixed-size blocks allocation, is the use of pools for memory management… preallocating a number of memory blocks with the same size called the memory pool. The application can allocate, access, and free blocks represented by handles at run time.

entries.name: Memory Protection Unit
entries.description: A Memory Protection Unit (MPU) is a processor component that enforces access control policies on memory regions to ensure the integrity, security, and proper operation of a computing system.

entries.name: Memory Read Event
entries.description: An event where a process retrieves data from a specific memory address, either from its own allocated space or that of another process.

entries.name: Memory Word
entries.description: A memory word is the natural unit of data used by a particular computer processor design; a fixed-size piece of data handled as a unit by the instruction set or the hardware of the processor.

entries.name: Memory Write Event
entries.description: An event where a process writes data to a memory address, storing new information or updating existing content.

entries.name: Message Analysis
entries.description: Analyzing email or instant message content to detect unauthorized activity.

entries.name: Message Authentication
entries.description: Authenticating the sender of a message and ensuring message integrity.

entries.name: Message Encryption
entries.description: Encrypting a message body using a cryptographic key.

entries.name: Message Hardening
entries.description: The application of security controls to user-to-user and system-to-system communications so messages remain confidential, unaltered, and verifiable while resisting injection, replay, and tampering.

entries.name: Message Transfer Agent
entries.description: A message transfer agent or mail transfer agent (MTA) or mail relay is software that transfers electronic mail messages from one computer to another using a client-server application architecture. An MTA implements both the client (sending) and server (receiving) portions of the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.

entries.name: Metadata
entries.description: Metadata is information which describes aspects of other information.

entries.name: Microcode
entries.description: Microcode is a computer hardware technique that interposes a layer of organization between the CPU hardware and the programmer-visible instruction set architecture of the computer. As such, the microcode is a layer of hardware-level instructions that implement higher-level machine code instructions or internal state machine sequencing in many digital processing elements.

entries.name: Microsoft HTML Application
entries.description: An HTML Application (HTA) is a Microsoft Windows program whose source code consists of HTML, Dynamic HTML, and one or more scripting languages supported by Internet Explorer, such as VBScript or JScript.

entries.name: Mobile Phone
entries.description: A mobile phone, cellular phone, cell phone, cellphone or hand phone, sometimes shortened to simply mobile, cell or just phone, is a portable telephone that can make and receive calls over a radio frequency link while the user is moving within a telephone service area. The radio frequency link establishes a connection to the switching systems of a mobile phone operator, which provides access to the public switched telephone network (PSTN). Modern mobile telephone services use a cellular network architecture and, therefore, mobile telephones are called cellular telephones or cell phones in North America. In addition to telephony, digital mobile phones (2G) support a variety of other services, such as text messaging, MMS, email, Internet access, short-range wireless communications (infrared,

entries.name: Modal Logic
entries.description: Modal logic is a collection of formal systems developed to represent statements about necessity and possibility. It plays a major role in philosophy of language, epistemology, metaphysics, and natural language semantics.

entries.name: Mode
entries.description: The most frequent value in the data set. This is the only central tendency measure that can be used with nominal data, which have purely qualitative category assignments.

entries.name: Model
entries.description: The model tactic is used to apply security engineering, vulnerability, threat, and risk analyses to digital systems. This is accomplished by creating and maintaining a common understanding of the systems being defended, the operations on those systems, actors using the systems, and the relationships and interactions between these elements.

entries.name: Model-based Policy Optimization
entries.description: Model-based policy optimization (MBPO) is a model-based, online, off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm. For more information on the different types of reinforcement learning agents

entries.name: Model-based Reinforcement Learning
entries.description: Model-based Reinforcement Learning refers to learning optimal behavior indirectly by learning a model of the environment by taking actions and observing the outcomes that include the next state and the immediate reward. The models predict the outcomes of actions and are used in lieu of or in addition to interaction with the environment to learn optimal policies.

entries.name: Model-based Value Iteration
entries.description: Value Iteration effectively reducesthe evaluation stage down to a single sweep of the states. Additionally, to improve things further, it combines the Policy Evaluation and Policy Improvement stages into a single update.

entries.name: Model-free Reinforcement Learning
entries.description: In reinforcement learning (RL), a model-free algorithm (as opposed to a model-based one) is an algorithm which does not use the transition probability distribution (and the reward function) associated with the Markov decision process (MDP),which, in RL, represents the problem to be solved. The transition probability distribution (or transition model) and the reward function are often collectively called the "model" of the environment (or MDP), hence the name "model-free". A model-free RL algorithm can be thought of as an "explicit" trial-and-error algorithm. An example of a model-free algorithm is Q-learning.

entries.name: Modem
entries.description: A modem -- a portmanteau of "modulator-demodulator" -- is a hardware device that converts data into a format suitable for a transmission medium so that it can be transmitted from one computer to another (historically along telephone wires). A modem modulates one or more carrier wave signals to encode digital information for transmission and demodulates signals to decode the transmitted information. The goal is to produce a signal that can be transmitted easily and decoded reliably to reproduce the original digital data. Modems can be used with almost any means of transmitting analog signals from light-emitting diodes to radio. A common type of modem is one that turns the digital data of a computer into modulated electrical signal for transmission over telephone lines and demodulated by another modem at the receiver side to recover the digital data.

entries.name: Moments
entries.description: With a probability distribution function, the first moment is the expected value, the second central moment is the variance, the third standardized moment is the skewness, and the fourth standardized moment is the kurtosis.

entries.name: Motion Detector
entries.description: An electrical device that utilizes a sensor to detect nearby motion.

entries.name: Motion Sensor Monitoring
entries.description: Monitoring events from motion detectors (e.g., passive IR, microwave, dual-technology) to detect presence or movement within protected areas.

entries.name: Mouse Input Device
entries.description: A computer mouse (plural mice or mouses) is a hand-held pointing device that detects two-dimensional motion relative to a surface. This motion is typically translated into the motion of a pointer on a display, which allows a smooth control of the graphical user interface of a computer. In addition to moving a cursor, computer mice have one or more buttons to allow operations such as selection of a menu item on a display. Mice often also feature other elements, such as touch surfaces and scroll wheels, which enable additional control and dimensional input.

entries.name: Move File
entries.description: A system call to rename or move a file.  Linux's rename() is an example of this kind of system call. Another way of handling it is to call a copy file system call followed by a delete file system call.

entries.name: Moving Average Model
entries.description: the moving-average model (MA model) is an approach for modeling univariate time series and specifies that the output variable is cross-correlated with a non-identical to itself random-variable.

entries.name: Multi-factor Authentication
entries.description: Requiring proof of two or more pieces of evidence in order to authenticate a user.

entries.name: Multilayer Perceptron Classification
entries.description: A multilayer perceptron (MLP) is a fully connected class of feedforward artificial neural network (ANN).An MLP consists of at least three layers of nodes: an input layer, a hidden layer and an output layer.

entries.name: Multimedia Document File
entries.description: Digital video files which often contain audio.

entries.name: Multimedia File
entries.description: A file that contains digital multimedia.

entries.name: Multiple Regression
entries.description: Multiple (linear) regression attempts to model the relationship between two or more explanatory variables and a response variable by fitting a linear equation to observed data.

entries.name: Multiple Regression Learning
entries.description: A supervised learning method that builds a multiple regression model using training data.

entries.name: Multivariate Analysis
entries.description: Multivariate statistics encompassed the simultaneous observation and analysis of more than one outcome variable, i.e., multivariate random variables.

entries.name: NIST SP 800-53 Control Catalog
entries.description: A NIST SP 800-53 control catalog provides the entire set of security and privacy controls for a version of NIST SP 800-53.

entries.name: NTFS Hard Link
entries.description: An NTFS hard link points to another file, and files share the same MFT entry (inode), in the same filesystem.

entries.name: NTFS Junction Point
entries.description: NTFS junction points are similar to NTFS symlinks but are defined only for directories. Only accepts local absolute paths.

entries.name: NTFS Link
entries.description: The NTFS filesystem defines various ways to link files, i.e. to make a file point to another file or its contents. The object being pointed to is called the target. There are three classes of NTFS links: (a) Hard links, which have files share the same MFT entry (inode), in the same filesystem; (b) Symbolic links, which record the path of another file that the links contents should show and can accept relative paths; and (c) Junction points, which are similar to symlinks but defined only for directories and only accepts local absolute paths

entries.name: NTFS Symbolic Link
entries.description: An NTFS symbolic link records the path of another file that the links contents should show. Can accept relative paths. SMB networking (UNC path) and directory support added in NTFS 3.1.

entries.name: NTP Broadcast Event
entries.description: An event where an NTP server broadcasts time synchronization messages to multiple clients simultaneously, enabling synchronization without individual request-response cycles.

entries.name: NTP Client Synchronization Event
entries.description: An event where an NTP client requests and adjusts its clock based on time synchronization data provided by an NTP server, ensuring alignment with a standard time source.

entries.name: NTP Control Message Event
entries.description: An event where an NTP client or server exchanges control messages used for diagnostic, monitoring, or administrative management of the NTP protocol, rather than time synchronization.

entries.name: NTP Event
entries.description: An event involving the Network Time Protocol (NTP), a protocol designed to synchronize the clocks of computer systems over packet-switched, variable-latency data networks, UDP as its transport protocol.

entries.name: NTP Server Response Event
entries.description: An event where an NTP server sends time synchronization data to a client, enabling the client to align its local clock with the server's reference time.

entries.name: NTP Symmetric Active Exchange Event
entries.description: An event where an NTP peer operating in symmetric active mode initiates clock synchronization messages to a peer in symmetric passive mode, enabling time synchronization between equal-status systems.

entries.name: NTP Symmetric Passive Exchange Event
entries.description: An event where an NTP peer operating in symmetric passive mode responds to clock synchronization messages initiated by a symmetric active peer, facilitating mutual timekeeping.

entries.name: Naive Bayes Classifier
entries.description: The Naïve Bayes classifier is a supervised machine learning algorithm, which is used for classification tasks, like text classification. It is also part of a family of generative learning algorithms, meaning that it seeks to model the distribution of inputs of a given class or category.

entries.name: Named Pipe
entries.description: In computing, a named pipe (also known as a FIFO for its behavior) is an extension to the traditional pipe concept on Unix and Unix-like systems, and is one of the methods of inter-process communication (IPC). The concept is also found in OS/2 and Microsoft Windows, although the semantics differ substantially. A traditional pipe is 'unnamed' and lasts only as long as the process. A named pipe, however, can last as long as the system is up, beyond the life of the process. It can be deleted if no longer used. Usually a named pipe appears as a file, and generally processes attach to it for IPC.

entries.name: Network
entries.description: A network is a group of computers that use a set of common communication protocols over digital interconnections for the purpose of sharing resources located on or provided by the network nodes. The interconnections between nodes are formed from a broad spectrum of telecommunication network technologies, based on physically wired, optical, and wireless radio-frequency methods that may be arranged in a variety of network topologies.

entries.name: Network Access Mediation
entries.description: Network access mediation is the control method for authorizing access to a system by a user (or a process acting on behalf of a user) communicating through a network, including a local area network, a wide area network, and the Internet.

entries.name: Network Agent
entries.description: A network agent is software installed on a network node or device that transmits information back to a collector agent or management system.  Kinds of network agents include SNMP Agent, IPMI agents, WBEM agents, and many proprietary agents capturing network monitoring and management information.

entries.name: Network Audio Streaming Resource
entries.description: A server that provides digital audio media content to users.

entries.name: Network Audio Visual Streaming Resource
entries.description: A server that provides digital audio-visual media content to users.

entries.name: Network Card Firmware
entries.description: Firmware that is installed on a network card (network interface controller).

entries.name: Network Connection Close Event
entries.description: An event where a network connection is closed.

entries.name: Network Connection Event
entries.description: An event related to the establishment, maintenance, or termination of a network connection.

entries.name: Network Connection Fail Event
entries.description: An event where a network connection attempt fails.

entries.name: Network Connection Listen Event
entries.description: An event where a network endpoint begins listening for new network connections.

entries.name: Network Connection Open Event
entries.description: An event where a network connection is successfully opened.

entries.name: Network Connection Refuse Event
entries.description: An event where a network connection is refused.

entries.name: Network Connection Reset Event
entries.description: An event where an attempt is made to establish a network connection.

entries.name: Network Device Event
entries.description: An event capturing the activity or state of network devices, such as Ethernet adapters, Wi-Fi modules, or virtual interfaces. These events highlight connectivity, configuration, or performance changes.

entries.name: Network Directory Resource
entries.description: A directory resource made available from one host to other hosts on a computer network.

entries.name: Network Event
entries.description: An event involving network communications within or between digital systems.

entries.name: Network File Resource
entries.description: A computer file resource made available from one host to other hosts on a computer network.

entries.name: Network File Share Resource
entries.description: A shared file resource, or network file share, is a computer file made available from one host to other hosts on a computer network. Network sharing is made possible by inter-process communication over the network. It includes both files and directories.

entries.name: Network Flow
entries.description: A summarization of network transactions between a client and server. It often summarizes bytes sent, bytes received, and protocol flags.

entries.name: Network Flow Sensor
entries.description: Monitors network traffic and produces summaries of data flows traversing the network.

entries.name: Network Frame
entries.description: A finite, self-delimited sequence of bits exchanged as one unit over a single data link. Formed by link-layer encapsulation, a frame typically begins with synchronization and control fields, carries a payload, ends with an integrity check, and is bounded from adjacent frames by explicit timing or delimiter symbols.

entries.name: Network Init Script File Resource
entries.description: A computer file resource made available from one host to other hosts on a computer network that is also an initialization script.

entries.name: Network Interface Card
entries.description: A network interface card (NIC, also known as a network interface controller, network adapter, LAN adapter or physical network interface, and by similar terms) is a computer hardware component that connects a computer to a computer network.

entries.name: Network Isolation
entries.description: Network Isolation techniques prevent network hosts from accessing non-essential system network resources.

entries.name: Network Link
entries.description: A network link is a link within the network layer, which is responsible for packet forwarding including routing through intermediate routers.

entries.name: Network Mapping
entries.description: Network mapping encompasses the techniques to identify and model the physical layer, network layer, and data exchange layers of the organization's network and their physical location, and determine allowed pathways through that network.

entries.name: Network Media Streaming Resource
entries.description: A server that provides digital media content to users.

entries.name: Network Multimedia Streaming Resource
entries.description: A server that provides digital multimedia content to users.

entries.name: Network Node
entries.description: In telecommunications networks, a node (Latin nodus, 'knot') is either a redistribution point or a communication endpoint. The definition of a node depends on the network and protocol layer referred to. A physical network node is an electronic device that is attached to a network, and is capable of creating, receiving, or transmitting information over a communications channel. A passive distribution point such as a distribution frame or patch panel is consequently not a node.

entries.name: Network Node Inventory
entries.description: Network node inventorying identifies and records all the network nodes (hosts, routers, switches, firewalls, etc.) in the organization's architecture.

entries.name: Network Packet
entries.description: A network packet is a formatted unit of data carried by a packet-switched network. Computer communications links that do not support packets, such as traditional point-to-point telecommunications links, simply transmit data as a bit stream. When data is formatted into packets, packet switching is possible and the bandwidth of the communication medium can be better shared among users than with circuit switching.

entries.name: Network Printer
entries.description: In computing, a network printer is a device that can be accessed over a network which makes a persistent representation of graphics or text, usually on paper. While most output is human-readable, bar code printers are an example of an expanded use for printers. The different types of printers include 3D printer, inkjet printer, laser printer, thermal printer, etc.  Note that not all printers are networked and the digital information to be printed must be passed either by removable media or as directly connecting the printer to a computer (e.g., by USB.)

entries.name: Network Protocol Analyzer
entries.description: Monitors and parses network protocols to extract values from various network protocol layers.

entries.name: Network Resource
entries.description: In computing, a shared resource, or network share, is a computer resource made available from one host to other hosts on a computer network. It is a device or piece of information on a computer that can be remotely accessed from another computer, typically via a local area network or an enterprise intranet, transparently as if it were a resource in the local machine.Network sharing is made possible by inter-process communication over the network.

entries.name: Network Resource Access
entries.description: Ephemeral digital artifact comprising a request of a network resource and any response from that network resource.

entries.name: Network Resource Access Mediation
entries.description: Control of access to organizational systems and services by users or processes over a network.

entries.name: Network Scanner
entries.description: A network scanner is a computer program used to retrieve usernames and info on groups, shares, and services of networked computers. This type of program scans networks for vulnerabilities in the security of that network. If there is a vulnerability with the security of the network, it will send a report back to a hacker who may use this info to exploit that network glitch to gain entry to the network or for other malicious activities. Ethical hackers often also use the information to remove the glitches and strengthen their network.

entries.name: Network Sensor
entries.description: A Network Sensor monitors network traffic and communication patterns.

entries.name: Network Service Application Process
entries.description: In computer networking, a network service is an application running at the network application layer and above, that provides data storage, manipulation, presentation, communication or other capability which is often implemented using a client-server or peer-to-peer architecture based on application layer network protocols. Clients and servers will often have a user interface, and sometimes other hardware associated with it.

entries.name: Network Session
entries.description: A network session is a temporary and interactive information interchange between two or more devices communicating over a network. A session is established at a certain point in time, and then 'torn down' - brought to an end - at some later point. An established communication session may involve more than one message in each direction. A session is typically stateful, meaning that at least one of the communicating parties needs to hold current state information and save information about the session history in order to be able to communicate, as opposed to stateless communication, where the communication consists of independent requests with responses. Network sessions may be established and implemented as part of protocols and services at the application, session, or transport layers of the OSI model.

entries.name: Network Time Server
entries.description: A network time server is a server computer that reads the actual time from a reference clock and distributes this information to its clients using a computer network. The time server may be a local network time server or an internet time server. The time server may also be a stand-alone hardware device. It can use NTP (RFC5905) or other protocols.

entries.name: Network Traffic
entries.description: Network traffic or data traffic is the data, or alternatively the amount of data, moving across a network at a given point of time.  Network data in computer networks is mostly encapsulated in network packets, which provide the load in the network.

entries.name: Network Traffic Analysis
entries.description: Analyzing intercepted or summarized computer network traffic to detect unauthorized activity.

entries.name: Network Traffic Analysis Software
entries.description: A packet analyzer, also known as packet sniffer, protocol analyzer, or network analyzer, is a computer program or computer hardware such as a packet capture appliance, that can intercept and log traffic that passes over a computer network or part of a network."

entries.name: Network Traffic Community Deviation
entries.description: Establishing baseline communities of network hosts and identifying statistically divergent inter-community communication.

entries.name: Network Traffic Filtering
entries.description: Restricting network traffic originating from any location.

entries.name: Network Traffic Policy Mapping
entries.description: Network traffic policy mapping identifies and models the allowed pathways of data at the network, transport, and/or application levels.

entries.name: Network Traffic Signature Analysis
entries.description: Analyzing network traffic and compares it to known signatures

entries.name: Network Video Streaming Resource
entries.description: A server that provides digital video media content to users.

entries.name: Network Vulnerability Assessment
entries.description: Network vulnerability assessment relates all the vulnerabilities of a network's components in the context of their configuration and interdependencies and can also include assessing risk emerging from the network's design as a whole, not just the sum of individual network node or network segment vulnerabilities.

entries.name: Non-Parametric Tests
entries.description: A non-parametric test relies is used when the underlying distribution of data is non-symmetric (non-normal distribution).

entries.name: Non-Person Entity
entries.description: An entity related to information technology with a digital identity that acts in cyberspace, but is not a human actor. This can include organizations, hardware objects (physical entities/devices), software objects (virtual/logical entities), and information artifacts.

entries.name: Non-monotonic Logic
entries.description: Non-monotonic logic is a formal logic whose conclusion relation is not monotonic. In other words, non-monotonic logics are devised to capture and represent defeasible inferences (cf. defeasible reasoning), i.e., a kind of inference in which reasoners draw tentative conclusions, enabling reasoners to retract their conclusion(s) based on further evidence.

entries.name: Nonlinear Regression
entries.description: Nonlinear regression is a form of regression analysis in which observational data are modeled by a function which is a nonlinear combination of the model parameters and depends on one or more independent variables.

entries.name: Nonlinear Regression Learning
entries.description: A supervised learning method that builds a non-linear regression model using training data.

entries.name: Null Pointer Checking
entries.description: Checking if a pointer is NULL.

entries.name: Numeric Pattern Matching
entries.description: Numeric pattern matching uses a pattern specification and sees if the numeric value matches that pattern--simple forms include exact matching and range matching.

entries.name: OS API Access Process
entries.description: An OS API function for interacting with processes.

entries.name: OS API Allocate Memory
entries.description: An OS API function that requests and allocates a region of memory for use by a process or application.

entries.name: OS API Connect Socket
entries.description: An OS API function that establishes a connection between a socket and a endpooint.

entries.name: OS API Copy Token
entries.description: An OS API function that creates a duplicate or copy of an existing security token.

entries.name: OS API Create File
entries.description: An OS API function that creates a file.

entries.name: OS API Create Process
entries.description: An OS API function that creates a new process within the system.

entries.name: OS API Create Socket
entries.description: An OS API function that creates a socket.

entries.name: OS API Create Thread
entries.description: An OS API function that creates a new thread of execution within a process.

entries.name: OS API Delete File
entries.description: An OS API function that removes a file from the file system.

entries.name: OS API Exec
entries.description: An OS API function that replaces the current process image with a new process image, executing a specified program.

entries.name: OS API Free Memory
entries.description: An OS API function that releases or deallocates memory that was previously allocated by the program.

entries.name: OS API Function
entries.description: A callable interface provided by an operating system that allows applications or other software components to interact with and utilize the underlying system resources, services, or functionalities.

entries.name: OS API Get System Time
entries.description: An OS API function that retrieves the current system time or timestamp.

entries.name: OS API Get Thread Context
entries.description: An OS API function that retrieves the execution context or state of a specific thread in a process.

entries.name: OS API Load Module
entries.description: An OS API function that loads a module into memory and makes it available for execution.

entries.name: OS API Move File
entries.description: An OS API function that moves or renames a file or directory from one location to another within the file system.

entries.name: OS API Open File
entries.description: An OS API function that opens a file for reading, writing, or both, and return a handle or descriptor that can be used to interact with the file.

entries.name: OS API Read File
entries.description: An OS API function that reads data from a file or input stream into memory.

entries.name: OS API Read Memory
entries.description: An OS API function that reads the contents of memory from a specific address or region.

entries.name: OS API Resume Process
entries.description: An OS API function that resumes the execution of a paused, stopped, or suspended process.

entries.name: OS API Resume Thread
entries.description: An OS API function that resumes the execution of a paused, stopped, or suspended thread.

entries.name: OS API Save Registers
entries.description: An OS API function that retrieves and saves the values of CPU registers for a specific process or thread.

entries.name: OS API Set Registers
entries.description: An OS API function that modifies the values of CPU registers.

entries.name: OS API Set Thread Context
entries.description: An OS API function that modifies the execution context of a thread.

entries.name: OS API Suspend Process
entries.description: An OS API function that pauses the execution of a process.

entries.name: OS API Suspend Thread
entries.description: An OS API function that pauses the execution of a thread.

entries.name: OS API System Function
entries.description: Indirect System calls are made through an OS-specific library (like glibc in Linux) that provides a higher-level API for the system calls.

entries.name: OS API Trace Process
entries.description: An OS API function that enables a program to monitor, control, or interact with the execution of a process.

entries.name: OS API Trace Thread
entries.description: An OS API function that enables a program to monitor, control, or interact with the execution of a thread.

entries.name: OS API Unload Module
entries.description: An OS API function that removes a previously loaded module from memory.

entries.name: OS API Write File
entries.description: An OS API function that writes data from a buffer in memory to a file or output stream.

entries.name: OS API Write Memory
entries.description: An OS API function that writes data into the memory space of another process or into specific regions of memory.

entries.name: OT Abort Command
entries.description: Commands a device to abort a service/program.

entries.name: OT Actuator
entries.description: An OT actuator is an industrial-grade actuator optimized for operational technology (OT) environments, such as SCADA or process-control systems. It tolerates harsher conditions, meets stricter safety and reliability standards, and integrates seamlessly with ICS protocols to enable real-time mechanical motion or adjustments in production lines and critical infrastructure.

entries.name: OT Alarm Message
entries.description: Report danger, hazards, or serious errors.

entries.name: OT Alarm Message Event
entries.description: Report danger, hazards, or serious errors.

entries.name: OT Change Control Program Command
entries.description: Commands a remote device to modify an existing control program.

entries.name: OT Change Control Program Command Event
entries.description: Commands a remote device to modify an existing control program.

entries.name: OT Change Data Command
entries.description: OT command that modifies existing data on a remote device.

entries.name: OT Change Data Command Event
entries.description: OT command that modifies existing data on a remote device.

entries.name: OT Connection Command
entries.description: Establish a network connection with a device.

entries.name: OT Connection Command Event
entries.description: Establish a network connection with a device.

entries.name: OT Control Command
entries.description: Command and control the managed process.

entries.name: OT Control Command Event
entries.description: Command and control the managed process.

entries.name: OT Control Function
entries.description: A function which accesses OT Control Variables

entries.name: OT Control Logic Process
entries.description: The instructions and algorithms within an OT Controller defined by user programming to interpret inputs, process information, and determine outputs.

entries.name: OT Control Program
entries.description: The file stored in controller memory that is used to operate the controller.

entries.name: OT Control Variable
entries.description: A control variable is the measurement of the physical condition of the device that influences the Process Variables.

entries.name: OT Controller
entries.description: An OT Controller is an industrial control device that automatically regulates one or more controlled variables in response to command inputs and real-time feedback signals.

entries.name: OT Controller Operating Mode
entries.description: The OT controller operating mode designates the specific, selectable state of an OT controller that delineates its operational behavior and governs access to engineering functions, commonly including Program, Run, Remote, Test, or Stop.

entries.name: OT Create Data Command
entries.description: OT command that creates data on a remote device.

entries.name: OT Create Data Command Event
entries.description: OT command that creates data on a remote device.

entries.name: OT Create New Control Program Command
entries.description: Commands a remote device to create an control program.

entries.name: OT Create New Control Program Command Event
entries.description: Commands a remote device to create an control program.

entries.name: OT Debug Command
entries.description: Investigate or analyze the current state of the system.

entries.name: OT Debug Command Event
entries.description: Investigate or analyze the current state of the system.

entries.name: OT Delete Control Program Command
entries.description: Commands a remote device to remove an existing control program.

entries.name: OT Delete Control Program Command Event
entries.description: Commands a remote device to remove an existing control program.

entries.name: OT Delete Data Command
entries.description: OT command that removes data on a remote device.

entries.name: OT Delete Data Command Event
entries.description: OT command that removes data on a remote device.

entries.name: OT Device Configuration Command
entries.description: Configure or administer managed devices.

entries.name: OT Device Configuration Command Event
entries.description: Configure or administer managed devices.

entries.name: OT Device Description Message
entries.description: Describe features, abilities, or performance of system components.

entries.name: OT Device Description Message Event
entries.description: Describe features, abilities, or performance of system components.

entries.name: OT Device Firmware Command
entries.description: Interact with the software responsible for low-level control of the system.

entries.name: OT Device Firmware Command Event
entries.description: Interact with the software responsible for low-level control of the system.

entries.name: OT Device Identification Message
entries.description: Identify devices on the network.

entries.name: OT Device Identification Message Event
entries.description: Identify devices on the network.

entries.name: OT Device Management Message
entries.description: Manage devices and their configurations.

entries.name: OT Device Management Message Event
entries.description: Manage devices and their configurations.

entries.name: OT Diagnostics Message
entries.description: Relay error, exception, alarm, or log information.

entries.name: OT Diagnostics Message Event
entries.description: Relay error, exception, alarm, or log information.

entries.name: OT Disconnect Remote Connection Command
entries.description: The Disconnect Request message is sent to the message receiver to indicate that the transmitter is terminating its TCP socket.

entries.name: OT Disconnect Remote Connection Command Event
entries.description: The Disconnect Request message is sent to the message receiver to indicate that the transmitter is terminating its TCP socket.

entries.name: OT Download Control Program Command
entries.description: Commands a remote device to download a control program.

entries.name: OT Download Control Program Command Event
entries.description: Commands a remote device to download a control program.

entries.name: OT Embedded Computer
entries.description: A ruggedized computational device, embedded in industrial control systems, designed to handle real-time tasks and environmental stressors common in OT.

entries.name: OT Engineering Software
entries.description: Software used in an industrial process to help engineers design, test, and maintain OT. This software enables the programming of OT controllers.

entries.name: OT Engineering Workstation
entries.description: An Engineering Workstation (EWS) is used to perform various maintenance, configuration, or diagnostics functions for a control system. The EWS will likely require dedicated application software to interface with various devices (e.g., RTUs, PLCs), and may be used to transfer data or files between the control system devices and other networks.

entries.name: OT Error Message
entries.description: An anticipated, reproducible defect occurred within the system.

entries.name: OT Error Message Event
entries.description: An anticipated, reproducible defect occurred within the system.

entries.name: OT Establish Remote Connection Command
entries.description: Used to establish an TCP/IP Connection to the target device.

entries.name: OT Establish Remote Connection Command Event
entries.description: Used to establish an TCP/IP Connection to the target device.

entries.name: OT Event
entries.description: A discrete occurrence within an operational technology environment that denotes a significant change in state, execution of a command, or transmission of information.

entries.name: OT Exception Message
entries.description: An unknown or anomalous condition occurred in the system.

entries.name: OT Exception Message Event
entries.description: An unknown or anomalous condition occurred in the system.

entries.name: OT Human Machine Interface
entries.description: Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs) are systems used by an operator to monitor the real-time status of an operational process and to perform necessary control functions, including the adjustment of device parameters.

entries.name: OT I/O Module
entries.description: An OT I/O Module is an industrial-grade interface designed for harsh Operational Technology (OT) environments. It reliably connects sensors and actuators to industrial control systems, ensuring precise, real-time data exchange in applications such as SCADA or ICS. Engineered for ruggedness and consistent performance, it can manage analog, digital, or other specialized signal types while enduring demanding conditions.

entries.name: OT Logic Variable
entries.description: A variable which directly affects a program running on an OT controller, involving an OT Process.

entries.name: OT Mode Switch
entries.description: Keyswitch or mode switch is the mechanism for changing the operating mode of an OT controller or device.

entries.name: OT Modify Control Program Command
entries.description: OT command that adds, removes, or changes, process data on a remote device.

entries.name: OT Modify Control Program Command Event
entries.description: OT command that adds, removes, or changes, process data on a remote device.

entries.name: OT Modify Device Configuration Command
entries.description: Modify device configuration.

entries.name: OT Modify Device Configuration Command Event
entries.description: Modify device configuration.

entries.name: OT Modify Device Operating Mode Command
entries.description: Modifies the running state of an application or program on a device.

entries.name: OT Modify Device Operating Mode Command Event
entries.description: Modifies the running state of an application or program on a device.

entries.name: OT Network
entries.description: A computer network which connects OT devices.

entries.name: OT Network Management Command
entries.description: Manage message routing or network connection mechanisms.

entries.name: OT Network Management Command Event
entries.description: Manage message routing or network connection mechanisms.

entries.name: OT Network Traffic
entries.description: Network traffic generated by operational technology devices, e.g., programmable logic controllers.

entries.name: OT Pause Command
entries.description: Commands a device to pause a service/program.

entries.name: OT Pause Command Event
entries.description: Commands a device to pause a service/program.

entries.name: OT Power Supply
entries.description: An OT power supply is a power supply whose control amplifier is optimized for signal-processing tasks rather than supplying mere steady-state power to a load. It is a self-contained combination of operational amplifiers, power amplifiers, and integral power circuits designed for higher-level operations in industrial or OT contexts.

entries.name: OT Process Data Command
entries.description: Manage data associated with a controlled process.

entries.name: OT Process Data Command Event
entries.description: Manage data associated with a controlled process.

entries.name: OT Process Data Historian
entries.description: A system used to collect and store data, including telemetry, events, alerts, and alarms about the operational process and supporting devices.

entries.name: OT Process Variable
entries.description: Process variables are the current actual measurement of the physical characteristics of a system. Common process variables include but are not limited to Temperature, Pressure, Level, and Flow.

entries.name: OT Program Mode Command
entries.description: Command that places the controller in a mode capable of reprogramming logic. This may or may not stop the program.

entries.name: OT Program Mode Command Event
entries.description: Command that places the controller in a mode capable of reprogramming logic. This may or may not stop the program.

entries.name: OT Proprietary Message
entries.description: Vendor specific and may not be publicly documented, or values left for device specific configuration.

entries.name: OT Proprietary Message Event
entries.description: Vendor specific and may not be publicly documented, or values left for device specific configuration.

entries.name: OT Protocol Message
entries.description: Packets generated by an operational technology protocol contain an OT protocol message.

entries.name: OT Read Command
entries.description: Read or retrieve data.

entries.name: OT Read Command Event
entries.description: Read or retrieve data.

entries.name: OT Read Device Configuration Command
entries.description: Read device configuration.

entries.name: OT Read Device Configuration Command Event
entries.description: Read device configuration.

entries.name: OT Read File Command
entries.description: Reads data in specified chunks or the contents of a specified file stored in the file device connected to the PC.

entries.name: OT Read File Command Event
entries.description: Reads data in specified chunks or the contents of a specified file stored in the file device connected to the PC.

entries.name: OT Read Time Command
entries.description: Read timing mechanisms.

entries.name: OT Read Time Command Event
entries.description: Read timing mechanisms.

entries.name: OT Read Value Command
entries.description: Reads the contents of the specified number of consecutive parameter areawords starting from the specified word.

entries.name: OT Read Value Command Event
entries.description: Reads the contents of the specified number of consecutive parameter areawords starting from the specified word.

entries.name: OT Remote Mode Command
entries.description: Command that places the controller in a mode capable of receiving read/write communication from a networked entity.

entries.name: OT Remote Mode Command Event
entries.description: Command that places the controller in a mode capable of receiving read/write communication from a networked entity.

entries.name: OT Run Command
entries.description: Commands a device to start or resume a service/program.

entries.name: OT Run Command Event
entries.description: Commands a device to start or resume a service/program.

entries.name: OT Scan Time
entries.description: An OT controller system variable that tracks the measured time it takes to read input status, apply logic, and write output values.

entries.name: OT Security Command
entries.description: Ensure confidentiality, integrity, or availability of system information.

entries.name: OT Security Command Event
entries.description: Ensure confidentiality, integrity, or availability of system information.

entries.name: OT Sensor
entries.description: An OT Sensor is an industrial-grade sensing device engineered for operational technology (OT) environments (e.g. SCADA, ICS). It measures physical variables—such as pressure, temperature, or flow—under demanding conditions, converting them into reliable signals for real-time monitoring and process control loops.

entries.name: OT Set Time Command
entries.description: Set timing mechanisms.

entries.name: OT Set Time Command Event
entries.description: Set timing mechanisms.

entries.name: OT Stop Command
entries.description: Commands a device to stop a service/program.

entries.name: OT Stop Command Event
entries.description: Commands a device to stop a service/program.

entries.name: OT Synchronize Time Command
entries.description: Used to align timing mechanisms.

entries.name: OT Synchronize Time Command Event
entries.description: Used to align timing mechanisms.

entries.name: OT Test Command
entries.description: Commands a  device to run a program in Test mode.

entries.name: OT Test Command Event
entries.description: Commands a  device to run a program in Test mode.

entries.name: OT Time Command
entries.description: Read, set, or calculate timing mechanisms.

entries.name: OT Time Command Event
entries.description: Read, set, or calculate timing mechanisms.

entries.name: OT Transport Configuration Command
entries.description: Configure transport settings for a communication channel.

entries.name: OT Transport Configuration Command Event
entries.description: Configure transport settings for a communication channel.

entries.name: OT Variable Access Restriction
entries.description: Assign read/write access controls on designated registers or data tags to prevent unauthorized writes.

entries.name: OT Watchdog Timer
entries.description: An OT Watchdog Timer is a software-based monitoring mechanism used in operational technology (OT) environments to continuously supervise the execution and responsiveness of critical control applications, devices, or communication links. It operates by requiring periodic “heartbeat” signals or status updates from monitored processes within a defined time window; if these signals are not received on time (indicating a hang, fault, or abnormal delay) the OT Watchdog Timer automatically triggers predefined safety or recovery actions, such as placing equipment in a fail-safe state, restarting services, generating alarms, or initiating controlled shutdowns.

entries.name: OT Write Command
entries.description: Write or store data.

entries.name: OT Write Command Event
entries.description: Write or store data.

entries.name: OWL
entries.description: The Web Ontology Language (OWL) is a family of knowledge representation languages for authoring ontologies.

entries.name: Object Eviction
entries.description: Terminate or remove an object from a host machine. This is the broadest class for object eviction.

entries.name: Object File
entries.description: An object file is a file that contains relocatable machine code.

entries.name: Offensive Tactic
entries.description: Per ATT&CK, these are defined as Tactical Goals, not Tactics per se. Many children also fit definition of tactics.  Some are neither tactics or tactical goals really (e.g., Execution, which is a useful grouping, but an action, not really a tactic or technique.

entries.name: Office Application
entries.description: An office application is one that is part of an application suite (e.g., Microsoft Office, Open Office).

entries.name: Office Application File
entries.description: A document file in a format associated with an d3f:OfficeApplication.

entries.name: One-time Password
entries.description: A one-time password is valid for only one user authentication.

entries.name: Open-source Developer
entries.description: An open-source developer contributes to the development, maintenance, or improvement of open-source projects.

entries.name: Open File
entries.description: For most file systems, a program initializes access to a file in a file system using the open system call. This allocates resources associated to the file (the file descriptor), and returns a handle that the process will use to refer to that file. In some cases the open is performed by the first access. During the open, the filesystem may allocate memory for buffers, or it may wait until the first operation. Various other errors which may occur during the open include directory update failures, un-permitted multiple connections, media failures, communication link failures and device failures.

entries.name: Operating Mode
entries.description: An operating mode designates the specific way a system, product, or service functions for a particular task, configuration, or phase of operation

entries.name: Operating Mode Monitoring
entries.description: Detects operating modes such as Program, Run, Remote, or Stop.

entries.name: Operating Mode Restriction
entries.description: Restricting unauthorized changes to the operating mode prevents devices from switching into inappropriate or vulnerable states during normal use.

entries.name: Operating System
entries.description: An operating system (OS) is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services for computer programs. All computer programs, excluding firmware, require an operating system to function. Time-sharing operating systems schedule tasks for efficient use of the system and may also include accounting software for cost allocation of processor time, mass storage, printing, and other resources.

entries.name: Operating System Clock
entries.description: An operating system clock is the primary software clock maintained by the operating system, representing the system's current time. It is used for timestamping files, scheduling tasks, and synchronizing processes.

entries.name: Operating System Configuration
entries.description: Information used to configure the services, parameters, and initial settings for an operating system.

entries.name: Operating System Configuration Component
entries.description: An component of the overall information necessary for the configuration of an operating system.

entries.name: Operating System Configuration File
entries.description: An operating system configuration file is a file used to configure the operating system.

entries.name: Operating System Configuration Modification Event
entries.description: An event that alters persistent operating-system configuration resources such as kernel options, registry keys, service definitions, or security policies; affecting system startup, hardware interfaces, or global security enforcement.

entries.name: Operating System Executable File
entries.description: An operating system executable is a critical executable that is part of the operating system, and without which, the operating system may not operate correctly.

entries.name: Operating System File
entries.description: An operating system file is a file that is part of, or used to store information about, the operating system itself.

entries.name: Operating System Log File
entries.description: An operating system log file records events that occur in an operating system.

entries.name: Operating System Monitoring
entries.description: The operating system software, for D3FEND's purposes, includes the kernel and its process management functions, hardware drivers, initialization or boot logic. It also includes and other key system daemons and their configuration. The monitoring or analysis of these components for unauthorized activity constitute **Operating System Monitoring**.

entries.name: Operating System Packaging Tool
entries.description: A software packaging tool oriented on building a software package for a particular operating system (e.g. rpmbuild.)

entries.name: Operating System Process
entries.description: An operating system process, or system process, is a process running to perform operating system functions.

entries.name: Operating System Shared Library File
entries.description: An operating system shared library file is a shared library file that is part of the operating system and that incorporates common operating system code for use by any application or to provide operating system services.

entries.name: Operational Activity Mapping
entries.description: Operational activity mapping identifies activities of the organization and the organization's suborganizations, groups, roles, and individuals that carry out the activities and then establishes the dependencies of the activities on the systems and people that perform those activities.

entries.name: Operational Activity Plan
entries.description: An activity is a specific behavior representing a set of actions that may be accomplished by an agent.

entries.name: Operational Dependency Mapping
entries.description: Operational dependency mapping identifies and models the dependencies of the organization's activities on each other and on the organization's performers (people, systems, and services.)  This may include modeling the higher- and lower-level activities of an organization forming a hierarchy, or layering, of the dependencies in an organization's activities.

entries.name: Operational Event
entries.description: An Operational Event is an action or occurrence within an organization's mission or business operations that happens over a period of time.

entries.name: Operational Logic Validation
entries.description: Validation of variable state in the context of the control logic of the operational application.

entries.name: Operational Process Monitoring
entries.description: Monitoring physical parameters and operator actions related to an operational environment.

entries.name: Operational Risk Assessment
entries.description: Operational risk assessment identifies and models the vulnerabilities of, and risks to, an organization's activities individually and as a whole.

entries.name: Operations Center Computer
entries.description: Mainframe computers or mainframes (colloquially referred to as "big iron") are computers used primarily by large organizations for critical applications; bulk data processing, such as census, industry and consumer statistics, and enterprise resource planning; and transaction processing. They are larger and have more processing power than some other classes of computers: minicomputers, servers, workstations, and personal computers.

entries.name: Optical Disc Image
entries.description: An optical disc image (or ISO image, from the ISO 9660 file system used with CD-ROM media) is a disk image that contains everything that would be written to an optical disc, disk sector by disc sector, including the optical disc file system.

entries.name: Optical Modem
entries.description: A modem that connects to a fiber optic network is known as an optical network terminal (ONT) or optical network unit (ONU). These are commonly used in fiber to the home installations, installed inside or outside a house to convert the optical medium to a copper Ethernet interface, after which a router or gateway is often installed to perform authentication, routing, NAT, and other typical consumer internet functions, in addition to "triple play" features such as telephony and television service.

entries.name: Orchestration Controller
entries.description: An orchestration server provides orchestration services that automate the configuration, coordination, and management of computer systems and software.

entries.name: Orchestration Server
entries.description: A d3f:Server which is involved with the orchestration of workloads or the execution of orchestrated workloads.

entries.name: Orchestration Worker
entries.description: A d3f:Server which receives commands from a d3f:OrchestrationController to execute workloads.

entries.name: Organization
entries.description: An organization with a defined mission/goal and a defined boundary, using systems to execute that mission, and with responsibility for managing its own risks and performance. An enterprise may consist of all or some of the following business aspects: acquisition, program management, human resources, financial management, security, and systems, information and mission management

entries.name: Organization Mapping
entries.description: Organization mapping identifies and models the people, roles, and groups with an organization and the relations between them.

entries.name: Outbound Internet DNS Lookup Traffic
entries.description: Outbound internet DNS lookup traffic is network traffic using the DNS protocol on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

entries.name: Outbound Internet Encrypted Remote Terminal Traffic
entries.description: Outbound internet encrypted remote terminal traffic is encrypted network traffic for a standard remote terminal protocol on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

entries.name: Outbound Internet Encrypted Traffic
entries.description: Outbound internet encrypted traffic is encrypted network traffic on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

entries.name: Outbound Internet Encrypted Web Traffic
entries.description: Outbound internet encrypted web traffic is network traffic using a standard web protocol on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

entries.name: Outbound Internet File Transfer Traffic
entries.description: Outbound internet file transfer traffic is file transfer traffic that is: (a) on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network, and (b) using a standard file transfer protocol.

entries.name: Outbound Internet Mail Traffic
entries.description: Outbound internet DNS lookup traffic is network traffic using a standard email protocol on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

entries.name: Outbound Internet Network Traffic
entries.description: Outbound internet network traffic is network traffic on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network.

entries.name: Outbound Internet RPC Traffic
entries.description: Outbound internet RPC traffic is RPC traffic that is: (a) on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network, and (b) using a standard RPC protocol.

entries.name: Outbound Internet Web Traffic
entries.description: Outbound internet web traffic is network traffic that is: (a) on an outgoing connection initiated from a host within a network to a host outside the network, and (b) using a standard web protocol.

entries.name: Outbound Network Traffic
entries.description: Outbound traffic is network traffic originating from a host of interest (client), to another host (server).

entries.name: Outbound Traffic Filtering
entries.description: Restricting network traffic originating from a private host or enclave destined towards untrusted networks.

entries.name: Output Device
entries.description: An output device is any piece of computer hardware equipment which converts information into human-readable form. It can be text, graphics, tactile, audio, and video.
