entries.description: x erases y: A technique x removes recorded data from storage device y creating space for new data.

entries.name: evaluated-by
entries.description: x evaluated-by y: The entity x is assessed and analyzed by entity y.

entries.name: evaluates
entries.description: x evaluates y: The entity x systematically assesses entity y to judge its state, quality, or risk.

entries.name: evicts
entries.description: x evicts y: The entity x forcibly removes entity y from the environment or resource where y was residing.

entries.name: exactly
entries.description: x exactly y: The entity x is identical to or fully corresponds to entity y.

entries.name: excises
entries.description: x excises y: Technique x removes a section of entity y.

entries.name: executed-by
entries.description: x executed-by y: The entity or function x is carried out, performed, or run by entity y.

entries.name: executes
entries.description: x executes y: The subject x takes the action of carrying out (executing) y, which is a single software module, function, or instruction.

entries.name: extends
entries.description: x extends y: The entity x extends the scope or range or area of entity y, especially in the sense of widening the range of applications.

entries.name: filters
entries.description: x filters y: A technique or agent x removes some specified set of entities from the content of a digital artifact y, by passing an artifact's content through a filter.  A filter is a device that removes something from whatever passes through it.

entries.name: forges
entries.description: x forges y: An technique or agent x counterfeits a digital artifact y, such as a fake credential, with the intent to deceive.

entries.name: hardens
entries.description: x hardens y: The entity x fortifies entity y to reduce its weaknesses so y can better withstand attack or failure.

entries.name: has-account
entries.description: x has-account y: The subject x has ownership or possession of some account y.

entries.name: has-agent
entries.description: x has-agent y: The event x occurs because agent y actively carries it out.

entries.name: has-dependent
entries.description: x has-dependent y: The entity x is relied upon or required by entity y.

entries.name: has-input
entries.description: x has-input y: An event x has input y iff y is an artifact that is present at the start of x, provides material or information required for x to begin, and during x either y's state is altered or the information content it bears is realized.

entries.name: has-link
entries.description: x has-link y: The d3fend analysis x has the link y.

entries.name: has-location
entries.description: x has-location y: The entity x is situated in a particular spot or position y.

entries.name: has-mediator
entries.description: x has-mediator y: The entity x relies on or is facilitated by entity y.

entries.name: has-operating-mode
entries.description: x has-operating-mode y: The entity x is currently operating in or has the potential to be in operating mode y.

entries.name: has-output
entries.description: x has-output y: An event x has output y iff y is an artifact that is present at the end of x, was not present in the same state at the start of x, and whose presence at the end is required for x to be considered complete; the change in state may arise either from a transformation of y itself or from the realization of the information content y bears.

entries.name: has-participant
entries.description: x has-participant y: The event x involves an object y as a participant, indicating that y plays some role in the event, whether actively, passively, or otherwise.

entries.name: has-recipient
entries.description: x has-recipient y: An agent y is the intended recipient and decoder of the information contained in communication x.

entries.name: has-sender
entries.description: x has-sender y: An agent y is the sender and encoder of the information contained in communication x.

entries.name: has-weakness
entries.description: x has-weakness y: The entity x exhibits a condition y that could, in some circumstances, lead to a vulnerability.

entries.name: hides
entries.description: x hides y: A technique or operation x conceals the digital artifact y.

entries.name: identified-by
entries.description: x identified-by y: The entity x is recognized or described by entity y.

entries.name: identifies
entries.description: x identifies y: The entity x recognizes or brings attention to entity y, making it distinct or clear through naming, description, or discovery.

entries.name: impairs
entries.description: x impairs y: The entity or action x hinders entity y by reducing its normal function, capacity, or availability.

entries.name: implemented-by
entries.description: x implemented-by y: The entity x is realized or brought into operation by entity y.

entries.name: implements
entries.description: x implements y: The entity x realizes entity y by putting its design or specification into effect.

entries.name: initiates
entries.description: x initiates y: The entity or action x starts or triggers entity or function y, bringing it into action.

entries.name: injects
entries.description: x injects y: The subject x takes the action of exploiting a security flaw by introducing (injecting) y, which is code or data that will change the course of execution or state of a computing process to an alternate course or state. Typically code injection is associated with adversaries intending the alternate course to facilitate a malevolent purpose; however, code injection can be unintentional or the intentions behind it may be good or benign.

entries.name: input-of
entries.description: x input-of y: An artifact x is input of an event y iff x participates at the start of y, provides the material or information required for y to begin, and during y either x's state is altered or the information content it bears is realized.

entries.name: installs
entries.description: x installs y: An entity x sets up digital artifact y for subsequent use.  For example, an installation program can install application software.

entries.name: instructed-by
entries.description: x instructed-by y: A subject x takes machine instructions from object y.

entries.name: instructs
entries.description: x instructs y: A subject x delivers machine instructions to object y.

entries.name: interprets
entries.description: x interprets y: The subject x interprets the executable script y. The definition of interprets here is 'Parse the source code and perform its behavior directly.'

entries.name: inventoried-by
entries.description: x inventoried-by y: The entity x is cataloged, recorded, or tracked by entity y.

entries.name: inventories
entries.description: x inventories y: The entity x systematically discovers entity y and records its presence and key details for tracking.

entries.name: invoked-by
entries.description: x invoked-by y: The entity x is called, triggered, or activated by entity y.

entries.name: invokes
entries.description: x invokes y: The subject x invokes a system service by use of an instruction object y that interrupts the program being executed and passes control to the operating system to perform that operation.

entries.name: isolates
entries.description: x isolates y: The technique or agent x sets digital artifact y apart from other digital artifacts, sequestering y.
Date of formal issuance of the resource.

entries.name: jams
entries.description: x jams y: The entity x deliberately introduces interfering energy that degrades, disrupts, blocks, or masks the information-bearing capability of the target y.

entries.name: kb-abstract
entries.description: x kb-abstract y: The reference x has the abstract y.

entries.name: kb-article
entries.description: The technique x has the kb-article y, where y is written in Markdown.

entries.name: kb-author
entries.description: x kb-author y: The reference x has some author y.

entries.name: kb-mitre-analysis
entries.description: x kb-mitre-analysis y: The reference x has the mitre d3fend analysis y.

entries.name: kb-organization
entries.description: x kb-organization y: The reference x was created or owned by the organization y.

entries.name: kb-reference-of
entries.description: x kb-is-example-of y: The reference x is an example of technique y.

entries.name: kb-reference-title
entries.description: x kb-reference-title y: The d3fend knowledge base reference x has the reference title string y.

entries.name: limits
entries.description: x limits y: The entity x specifies a designated limit beyond which some entity y cannot function or must be terminated.

entries.name: loaded-by
entries.description: x loaded-by y: The entity x is brought into memory by entity y.

entries.name: loads
entries.description: x loads y: The technique or process x transfers a software from storage y to a computer's memory for subsequent execution.

entries.name: manages
entries.description: x manages y: The technique or agent x watches and directs the use of digital artifact y.

entries.name: mapped-by
entries.description: x mapped-by y: The entity x is linked to another entity by entity y.

entries.name: maps
entries.description: x maps y: The entity x discovers and records how entity y is arranged and interconnected.

entries.name: may-access
entries.description: x may-access y: The entity x may access the thing y; that is, 'x accesses y' may be true.

entries.name: may-add
entries.description: x may-add y: The entity x may add the thing y; that is, 'x adds y' may be true.

entries.name: may-be-associated-with
entries.description: x may-be-associated-with y: The subject x and object y may be associated in some way.

entries.name: may-be-tactically-associated-with
entries.description: x may-be-tactically-associated-with y: the defensive action x may be a tactic that counters offensive action y.

entries.name: may-block
entries.description: x may-block y: The entity x may block the thing y; that is, 'x blocks y' may be true.

entries.name: may-contain
entries.description: to potentially have as contents or constituent parts; comprise; include.

entries.name: may-corrupt
entries.description: x may-corrupt y: The entity x may corrupt y's information content; that is, 'x corrupts y' may be true.

entries.name: may-create
entries.description: x may-create y: The entity x may create the entity y; that is, 'x creates y' may be true.

entries.name: may-execute
entries.description: x may-execute y: The subject x may take the action of carrying out (executing) y, which is a single software module, function, or instruction.

entries.name: may-interpret
entries.description: x may-interpret y: The entity x may interpret the thing y; that is, 'x interprets y' may be true.

entries.name: may-invoke
entries.description: x may-invoke y: The entity x may invoke the thing y; that is, 'x invokes y' may be true.

entries.name: may-modify
entries.description: x may-modify y: The entity x may modify the thing y; that is, 'x modifies y' may be true.

entries.name: may-produce
entries.description: x may-produce y: The entity x may produce the thing y; that is, 'x produces y' may be true.

entries.name: may-run
entries.description: x may-run y: The entity x may run the thing y; that is, 'x runs y' may be true.

entries.name: may-transfer
entries.description: x may-transfer y: The entity x may send the thing y; that is, 'x transfers y' may be true.

entries.name: mediates-access-to
entries.description: x mediates-access-to y: The entity x controls and brokers requests to reach entity y, enforcing the access rules that allow or deny it.
Date on which the resource was changed.

entries.name: modified-by
entries.description: x modified-by y: The entity x is changed by entity y.

entries.name: modifies
entries.description: x modifies y: A technique or agent x causes a digital object y to change; become different; or undertake a transformation.  Afterwards, the data or state held by a digital object is changed.

entries.name: modifies-part
entries.description: x modifies-part y: The entity x modifies a part of y.  [Note: This is a rolification property for the rule 'if one modifies a part of a whole, they modify the whole.'  Reasoning for this and similar semantics to come are under evaluation and not part of current d3fend inferences.]

entries.name: monitors
entries.description: x monitors y: The technique or agent x keep tabs on, keeps an eye on, or keeps the digital artifact y under surveillance.

entries.name: narrower
entries.description: x narrower y: The entity x represents a more specific or focused concept than entity y.

entries.name: narrower-transitive
entries.description: x narrower-transitive y: The entity x represents a more specific concept than entity y, including indirect or hierarchical relationships where x is a subset of y through intermediate entities.

entries.name: neutralizes
entries.description: x neutralizes y: The technique x makes the execution of actions of y ineffective by preventing or counterbalancing the effect of y.

entries.name: obfuscates
entries.description: x obfuscates y: The technique x makes the digital artifact y unclear or obscure.  Typically obfuscation is a way to hide a digital artifact from discovery, use, or both.

entries.name: operates
entries.description: x operates y: The entity x enables, activates, or controls the functioning or behavior of object y (operated entity), typically in accordance with the design or intended use of the operated entity.
x operating-system y: The product x is supported on operating system y.

entries.name: originates-from
entries.description: x originates-from y: The digital event or artifact x began its network transit from a physical location y.

entries.name: output-of
entries.description: x output-of y: An artifact x is output of an event y iff x must be present when y concludes, was absent in the same state when x began, and y counts as complete only when x is available at its end.

entries.name: owns
entries.description: x owns y: The subject x has ownership or possession of some object y.

entries.name: participates-in
entries.description: x participates-in y: The object x takes part in the event y, signifying that x contributes to or is affected by the event's occurrence in some way.

entries.name: powered-by
entries.description: x powered-by y: x obtains its essential energy or force from y to perform its function or remain active.

entries.name: powers
entries.description: x powers y: x furnishes y with the energy or force required for y's functionality or operation.

entries.name: preceded-by
entries.description: x preceded-by y: The event or action x occurs after event or action y in time.

entries.name: precedes
entries.description: x precedes y: The event or action x occurs before event or action y in time.

entries.name: pref-label
entries.description: x pref-label y: The preferred display value for x is y in d3fend tools.

entries.name: prescribed-by
entries.description: x prescribed-by y: y provides a directive specification for x (i.e., y serves as a rule or guide for x).

entries.name: prescribes
entries.description: x prescribes y: x provides a directive specification for y (i.e., x serves as a rule or guide for how y is intended to occur or be made).

entries.name: process-ancestor
entries.description: x process-ancestor y: The process y is a process ancestor of process x, indicating one or more process creation events were conducted at process y and subsequently created process x.

entries.name: process-command-line-arguments
entries.description: x process-command-line-arguments y: The process x has the process command line arguments data y.

entries.name: process-data-property
entries.description: x process-data-property y: The process x has the data property y.

entries.name: process-environmental-variables
entries.description: x process-environment-variables y: The process x has the process environmental variables data y.

entries.name: process-identifier
entries.description: x process-identifier y: The process x has the process identifier y.

entries.name: process-image-path
entries.description: x process-image-path y: The filepath y is the process image path for the process x, indicating the path to the resource from which the process's image was loaded.

entries.name: process-parent
entries.description: x process-parent y: The process y created the process x (directly) with a create process event.

entries.name: process-property
entries.description: x process-property y: The process x has the a process-property y.  This is generalization for specific process object properties.

entries.name: process-security-context
entries.description: x process-security-context y: The process x has the process security context data y.

entries.name: process-user
entries.description: x process-user y: The process x has been executed by the user y.

entries.name: produced-by
entries.description: x produced-by y: The entity x is created by entity y.

entries.name: produces
entries.description: x produces y: The subject entity x or process produces a data object y, which may be discrete digital object or a stream (e.g., a stream such as network traffic.)

entries.name: provider
entries.description: x provider y: A provider y is an entity that supplies a service, system, or data resources to a dependent entity x.
Date of publication of the resource.

entries.name: quarantines
entries.description: x quarantines y: Technique x moves entity y to a place of isolation.

entries.name: queries
entries.description: x queries y: The entity x requests information or data from entity y.

entries.name: reads
entries.description: x reads y: The subject x takes the action of reading from a digital source y to acquire data and placing it into volatile memory for processing.

entries.name: receives
entries.description: x receives y: The subject x acquires object y from a communication medium and transfers y into its local context for storage or processing.

entries.name: recorded-in
entries.description: x recorded-in y: The event x is documented, logged, or otherwise preserved within the digital artifact y, which stores or encodes relevant data about the event.

entries.name: records
entries.description: x records y: The digital artifact x makes a record of events y; set down in permanent form.

entries.name: regenerates
entries.description: x regenerates y: The entity x discards the current digital artifact y and creates a new version that serves the same function.

entries.name: related
entries.description: x related y: x has a symmetric associative relation to y.

entries.name: release-date
entries.description: x release-date y: The object x has the release-date y.

entries.name: restores
entries.description: x restores y: The entity x returns entity y to its known-good or previous state.

entries.name: restricted-by
entries.description: x restricted-by y: The entity x is limited, constrained, or regulated by entity y.

entries.name: restricts
entries.description: x restricts y: The entity x bounds the use of entity y.

entries.name: resumes
entries.description: x resumes y: The agent or technique x continues a previous action on entity y. Usually occurs after suspension on y.

entries.name: risk-impact
entries.description: Risk impact rating, expressed on a numeric scale from 1 (lowest impact) to 5 (highest impact) in the context of a 5x5 risk matrix. Impact is used here as a synonym for consequence, another popular term used in risk analysis.

entries.name: risk-likelihood
entries.description: Risk likelihood rating, expressed on a numeric scale from 1 (lowest likelihood) to 5 (highest likelihood) in the context of a 5x5 risk matrix.

entries.name: runs
entries.description: x runs y: To carry out a process or program y, as on a computer or a machine x; where y may be a large software assembly or a specific module or instruction.  Examples: "run a new program on the Mac"; "the computer runs the application software".

entries.name: semantic-relation
entries.description: x semantic-relation y: The entity x is conceptually or meaningfully connected to entity y.

entries.name: signed-by
entries.description: x signed-by y: The digital artifact x includes a signature generated by the entity y, certifying the authenticity and integrity of x. This relationship indicates that x has undergone a validation process by y, using cryptographic measures to ensure that x is trustworthy and unaltered since the signing by y.

entries.name: signs
entries.description: x signs y: The entity x applies a digital signature to the digital artifact y, thereby asserting its validity, integrity, and authenticity. Typically, this involves cryptographic techniques to securely bind the signature to y, ensuring that y's contents have not been altered and are authentic as endorsed by x.

entries.name: spoofs
entries.description: x spoofs y: The technique x creates a fake instance of a digital artifact y; that is, y is a decoy, fake, or counterfeit.

entries.name: strengthens
entries.description: x strengthens y: The technique x makes digital artifact y resistant (to harm or misuse.)

entries.name: summarizes
entries.description: x summarizes y: The sensor x summarizes a set y of events concerning digital artifacts over time.

entries.name: suspends
entries.description: x suspends y: The agent or technique x pauses entity y.

entries.name: synonym
entries.description: an equivalent term.

entries.name: t-SNE Clustering
entries.description: T-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) is a statistical method for visualizing high-dimensional data by giving each datapoint a location in a two or three-dimensional map.

entries.name: terminates
entries.description: x terminates y: The technique x brings to an end or halt to some activity y.
The text of the document (i.e., terms of license.)
A name given to the resource.

entries.name: transmits
entries.description: x transmits y: The subject x actively emits object y onto a communication medium, rendering y observable and available for reception on that medium.

entries.name: unloads
entries.description: x unloads y: The technique or artifact performs the action of unloading some artifact (applications, kernel modules, or hardware drivers, etc.) from a computer's memory.

entries.name: unmounts
entries.description: x unmounts y: An operation x removes the access via computer system's file system the availability of files and directories on storage artifact y.  Unmounts reverse or undo prior mount operations.

entries.name: updates
entries.description: x updates y: The technique x updates the software for component y.

entries.name: use-limits
entries.description: x use-limits y: The entity x specifies a designated number of uses beyond which some entity y cannot function or must be terminated.

entries.name: used-by
entries.description: x used-by y: The inverse of y uses x.

entries.name: uses
entries.description: x uses y: The entity x puts into service a resource or implement y; makes y work or employ for a particular purpose or for its inherent or natural purpose.
Date (often a range) of validity of a resource.

entries.name: validated-by
entries.description: x validated-by y: The digital artifact x has its authenticity and correctness confirmed or verified by the technique, operation, or agent y.

entries.name: validates
entries.description: x validates y: The technique x proves the digital artifact y is valid; that is, x shows or confirms the validity of y.

entries.name: verifies
entries.description: x verifies y: The technique x confirms the truth of a digital artifact y.
x version y: The product or service x has the version y.

entries.name: Reconnaissance
entries.description: Adversary gathers information about the target space system including orbital parameters, frequency bands, and ground station locations.

entries.name: Resource Development
entries.description: Adversary establishes resources to support space operations targeting, including jamming equipment and cyber tools.

entries.name: Initial Access - Ground Segment
entries.description: Adversary gains access to ground control systems via phishing, vulnerable internet-facing services, or supply chain compromise.

entries.name: Initial Access - Space Segment
entries.description: Adversary gains access to the space vehicle via malicious commands over RF link or compromised firmware.

entries.name: Execution - Command Injection
entries.description: Adversary injects unauthorized commands into the spacecraft command queue.

entries.name: Persistence - Firmware Modification
entries.description: Adversary modifies spacecraft firmware to maintain persistent access across power cycles.

entries.name: Defense Evasion - Safe Mode Trigger
entries.description: Adversary intentionally triggers safe mode to disrupt operations or mask malicious activity.

entries.name: Denial of Service - Jamming
entries.description: Adversary jams the uplink or downlink frequencies to deny communication with the spacecraft.

entries.name: Exfiltration - Downlink Interception
entries.description: Adversary intercepts unencrypted downlink data to collect telemetry, imagery, or sensitive payload data.

entries.name: Impact - Orbit Modification
entries.description: Adversary sends unauthorized commands to alter spacecraft orbit, potentially causing collision or mission failure.

entries.name: Lateral Movement - Ground to Space
entries.description: Adversary pivots from ground segment compromise to issue commands to the space segment.

entries.name: Collection - Telemetry Harvesting
entries.description: Adversary collects spacecraft telemetry to understand system state, vulnerabilities, and operations schedule.

entries.name: Unauthorized Access to Ground Station
entries.description: Adversary gains unauthorized access to ground station systems through exploiting vulnerabilities in internet-facing services, social engineering, or physical intrusion.

entries.name: Command Link Spoofing
entries.description: Adversary transmits fake command signals to the spacecraft, potentially causing incorrect maneuvers, mode changes, or payload activation.

entries.name: Telemetry Link Interception
entries.description: Adversary intercepts spacecraft telemetry downlink to gather intelligence on spacecraft health, orbit parameters, and operational status.

entries.name: GPS/GNSS Spoofing
entries.description: Adversary broadcasts counterfeit GNSS signals to mislead spacecraft navigation systems, causing position and timing errors.

entries.name: Supply Chain Compromise
entries.description: Adversary introduces malicious components or software during spacecraft or ground system manufacturing and integration phases.

entries.name: Denial of Service via RF Jamming
entries.description: Adversary transmits high-power signals on spacecraft communication frequencies to deny or degrade communication links.

entries.name: Onboard Software Modification
entries.description: Adversary exploits a vulnerability in the spacecraft onboard computer to modify flight software, affecting mission operations.

entries.name: Insider Threat
entries.description: Malicious or negligent insider with authorised access to space systems causes harm through data theft, sabotage, or unintended misconfiguration.

entries.name: Inter-Satellite Link Attack
entries.description: Adversary targets crosslink communications between satellites in a constellation to disrupt relay operations or inject false data.

entries.name: Cryptographic Key Compromise
entries.description: Adversary obtains cryptographic keys used for securing command uplinks or telemetry downlinks, enabling decryption or command forgery.

entries.name: Mission Data Manipulation
entries.description: Adversary tampers with science or imagery data collected by the spacecraft payload, undermining mission integrity.

entries.name: Replay Attack on Telecommands
entries.description: Adversary records legitimate telecommand sequences and replays them to cause unintended spacecraft actions.
